source: a16z Podcast — AI demand outrunning compute supply; frontier-lab revenue is self-determined, reinvestment math, not necessarily winner-take-all
summary: Compute infrastructure paybacks are sub-one-year, making this one of the best capital deployment opportunities Baker has seen in his career
summary_extended: Baker argues that AI compute infrastructure represents one of the best capital deployment opportunities of his career, citing sub-one-year equity paybacks driven by customer prepayment structures. Specifically, disclosures from Nebius and CoreWeave imply that a 1GW data center costing roughly $50B receives 50-60% upfront from customers (~$25-30B), with the remainder monetized at spot GPU rental rates of $2-8/hour, yielding 9-10 month paybacks. The financing structure further compresses the equity requirement: alternative asset managers like Blackstone, KKR, and Apollo are financing Nvidia GPUs at low cost, meaning a $50B data center may require only ~$15B in equity with $35B financed, making true equity paybacks potentially well inside one year. Baker notes SpaceX builds large clusters even faster with faster paybacks, reinforcing the structural advantage. The investment implication is that companies able to deploy tens or hundreds of billions into GPU infrastructure at these economics — and the financiers enabling that leverage — are in an exceptionally favorable position.
